title: With Songs and Honors Sounding Loud
description: With Songs and Honors Sounding Loud in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 853 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Seasons”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: With songs and hon-ors sound-ing loud, Ad-dress the Lord on high; O'er all the heavens he spreads his cloud, And wa-ters veil the sky.

lines: With songs and honors sounding loud,
O'er all the heavens he spreads his cloud,
He sends his showers of blessings down,
He makes the grass the mountains crown,
His steady councils change the face
He bids the sun cut short his race,
On us his providence has shone,
O, may our lips and lives make known

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
